items.title: The Axis That Counts by Ratio
items.theme: what a logarithmic axis makes visible, what it hides, and what using one has already decided
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: A cat-tier thread break with a deliberately plausible false anchor: the paragraph contains something a hurried reader will accept as the first restriction, which is what stops a pronoun-spotting heuristic from solving the item.

items.title: The Line the Buildings Forget
items.theme: why the lines of old streets outlive every building that has ever stood on them
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: The outlier is the only fully concrete sentence in an abstract set, which makes it feel like the example the paragraph is missing. The branch it takes is design for comfort; the paragraph's road is ownership and consent.

items.title: The Filing Cabinet
items.theme: the dispute between a right of removal and the value of the record recast, since in the cases that arise nothing is deleted and only retrieval changes, so the right is an attempt to restore by rule the friction the filing cabinet used to supply, which narrows it to a claim about what a machine will offer unasked and obliges somebody to decide, name by name, which enquirers count as neighbours
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-06
items.reviewer_notes: The passage's pivot is that both parties to a famous quarrel share a premise that the cases do not support, so the distractors are built mostly out of the quarrel the author has stepped away from. The last paragraph does three jobs in quick succession, names two costs, grants the other side a point and then measures the grant, and the two hardest questions are decided there.

items.title: The Marble on the Front
items.theme: the century-old quarrel over whether advertising informs or persuades broken by an analogy with the marble front of a bank, where the message is carried by the expenditure rather than by the content, and then bounded at the joint the analogy exposes, since the expense certifies only that the seller expects to meet the buyer again and therefore certifies nothing in a market of single sales
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-06
items.reviewer_notes: The analogy is pressed for a paragraph and then deliberately broken, and the break is where three of the four questions are decided. The last paragraph grants the persuasion camp two things in a row and then refuses their conclusion, which makes the concession itself available as a distractor for the structural question.

items.title: Staying for the Sentence
items.theme: the requirement that a civil disobedient accept his punishment defended neither by sincerity nor by fidelity to law but by what submission does to the act, since remaining and taking the consequence is what keeps the claim addressed to the community that is being asked to think again, which makes the requirement constitutive rather than evidential and suspends it wherever the penalty is itself the injustice complained of
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-06
items.reviewer_notes: The hard move is that submission is treated as constitutive rather than evidential, which most readers have no slot for, so several distractors offer it as a test, a proof or a payment. The final paragraph applies the definition to three cases, states a limit and then grants one of the rejected defences a real point, and the purpose question is decided by whether a reader kept the limit inside the purpose.

items.title: The Cousin Who Knows the Agent
items.theme: a ceiling on a price described through the queue rather than through the crossing lines, so that the interesting question becomes who obtained the good and what they handed over, with the answer that the price was paid in another currency and that this currency, unlike money, is spent without being received by anybody
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-06
items.reviewer_notes: A short passage built as a question and its answer, where the payoff is not the shortage but the difference between a payment that is transferred and one that is merely spent. The last paragraph concedes a redistributive purpose and then refuses the inference readers most want to draw, which is where the main idea question is decided.

items.title: The Plate Spoiled Overnight
items.theme: the maxim that chance favours the prepared mind held against the objection that it is assembled from its successes and defined by its outcome, and settled by giving up the claim that preparation makes accidents likelier while keeping the claim that a precise expectation is what lets an anomaly be taken for a finding rather than a fault, whose only practical consequence is about how a laboratory spends time
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-06
items.reviewer_notes: A dialectic in which the author gives the objectors half of the original claim and keeps the other half, so both the famous maxim and its debunking are available as wrong answers to the main idea question. The final paragraph is where the practical consequence lives, and it is deliberately smaller and less quotable than the moral the histories draw.

items.title: The Empty Road at Night
items.theme: obedience to law explained by the acknowledged standing of the body issuing a demand rather than by the price of disobeying it, supported by an expected penalty too small to produce the observed compliance, by falls and rises that track fairness while enforcement stands still, and by obedience to rules the obedient think mistaken, with the sanction granted a constituent role and refused a motivating one
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-06
items.reviewer_notes: A thesis with three supports and a final paragraph that gives the rejected account two things before refusing it a third, which is what keeps the attitude question genuinely hard: the author is neither hostile nor neutral but demoting. The EXCEPT question is built from the three supports plus a fourth claim that is plausible in the world and absent from the page.

items.title: The Word in Quotation Marks
items.theme: two accounts of what became of the idea of progress after the twentieth century, one holding that the evidence destroyed it and one that it merely changed address from the moral to the technical, adjudicated by granting the second the better description and the first the better sense of the loss, since a claim about departments cannot license the argument that a present cost is redeemed by the direction of the whole
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-06
items.reviewer_notes: The adjudication splits rather than picks, giving each account half of the verdict, and the final paragraph then refuses two comfortable conclusions in a row: that the loss was regrettable and that nothing was lost but a word. The tone question is built on the second of those refusals, which readers reliably hear as either mourning or relief.

items.title: The Reasons She Could Say
items.theme: a choice that reverses itself while the reasons for it are being spoken aloud, explained neither as deliberation correcting an instinct nor as talk overriding one, but as a selection effect in the medium, since producing reasons composes a preference out of whatever will go into a sentence, which makes the standard advice to list one's reasons conditional on whether the choice will later have to be defended to somebody who was not there
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-06
items.reviewer_notes: The opening scene is engineered so that both folk explanations fail on the same detail, that the choice moved while the list did not, and every distractor in the set is one of those explanations restored. The final paragraph concedes that the wordless preference may be worth nothing and then refuses the inference that the two preferences are therefore interchangeable, which is where the implication question is decided.

items.title: The Number He Will Give You
items.theme: the usual line between risk and uncertainty redrawn, since a probability can always be supplied and what actually separates the two cases is whether the list of outcomes is closed, which splits forecasting failure into a wrong number that more observation can repair and a short list that no amount of observation can lengthen
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-06
items.reviewer_notes: Short, dense and built on one substitution: not whether the odds are known but whether the list is closed. The final paragraph concedes that the partition is not clean and then refuses the practice the concession might seem to excuse, which is where the purpose question separates from the definitional reading.

items.title: The Rate the Bank Pays
items.theme: the familiar complaint that prices climb quickly and fall slowly answered by pointing out that appetite is symmetrical and cannot produce an asymmetry, and explained instead by the buyer's information, since a rise in costs is public and removes the point of searching while a fall is invisible at the counter and nobody searches until he learns there is something to find
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-06
items.reviewer_notes: The argument turns on a single logical observation, that a constant cannot explain a difference, and everything else follows from it. The author is lightly amused rather than measured, which is deliberate: the tone options are not a caricature pair flanking a middle, and the correct one names an attitude with a definite colour.

items.title: The Threshold and Who It Guards
items.theme: why a two-thirds requirement is partial between times rather than between people
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: A medium-tier item in which the outlier is the sentence most readers would use to introduce the topic. The core is short, tight and entirely about one mechanism, so the general claim can be shown to carry no link.

items.title: The Box Everybody Ticks
items.theme: how a doubtful assumption about assent was replaced by a stored record of a click
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: A narrative about a doctrine's small steps, with an outlier that offers the aggregate importance of the practice. The item rewards building the sequence first: once the four stages are in order, the statistic has no stage to occupy.

items.title: The Road Is the Observance
items.theme: why the journey rather than the destination is the thing a pilgrimage performs
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: An easy-tier item where the outlier shares the setting and nothing else. The decoy teaches that a sentence introducing a quarrel can still be the sentence that proves the paragraph's point.

items.title: The Discount That Never Arrives
items.theme: why a payment made to buyers ends up wherever supply is slowest to grow
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: An easy-tier stance break placed where indignation is most natural. The core is careful and conditional throughout, which is what makes the one accusing sentence impossible to fit.

items.title: The Room Where the Case Is Read
items.theme: how a hospital ethics committee works through one case, and what it hands back
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: A foundation item whose core is a plain sequence, so the learner can see the shape of the paragraph at a glance and feel the one sentence that is not part of the morning being described.

items.title: The Wrong Name That Will Not Move
items.theme: why a word on the tip of the tongue is blocked by the near miss that keeps arriving instead
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: A medium-tier thread break with a deliberately countable false anchor. The item teaches the learner to check what a paragraph has actually enumerated rather than what it feels as though it enumerated.

items.title: The Patients Who Were Always Going to Be Well
items.theme: why lowering the line for a diagnosis improves survival figures without lengthening anybody's life
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: The outlier is the sentence a reader wants in an argument made of numbers: a real patient doing something. It illustrates adherence, which the argument never mentions, and that is the whole test.

items.title: Three Volumes and a Subscription
items.theme: how a lending arrangement set the length of a novel, and what happened to the form when the arrangement ended
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: A narrative whose outlier is its own moral. The item is built to punish the reader who assembles a paragraph around the most quotable sentence rather than around the sequence of events.

items.title: The Bone That Is Not Lighter
items.theme: why a flying bird's hollow bones answer a problem of stiffness rather than one of weight
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: An elite scope item in which the shared word does the camouflage. Both the core and the outlier are about mass in flight, but one is about the mass of a whole bird over a journey and the other about where mass sits within a single bone.

items.title: A Guarantee You Cannot Cash
items.theme: what a proof of existence that produces no example does and does not license
items.reviewer_notes: The forward clue is a definite noun phrase — 'The contradiction' — that nothing but the missing sentence introduces; the backward clue is the class of proofs the first sentence names, which 'the usual route' has to be the route of. The opening slot is the live rival and it widens the paragraph from one kind of proof to proof in general.

items.title: The Officer Who Could Stop Nobody
items.theme: why a traffic officer is obeyed: authority as something granted, not imposed
items.reviewer_notes: A gentle two-direction item: 'That grant' has exactly one antecedent in the paragraph, and the closing sentence's 'the cheaper of the two' cannot be read until the two have been named. Suitable as an early placement item.

items.title: Who Signs and Who Pays
items.theme: why the law's named payer of a charge is not the party who bears it, and what settles the share
items.reviewer_notes: Premium: the sentence could follow any of three sentences on topic, and only two words decide it — 'the same rule', which needs a rule and not merely a process, and 'there' in the next sentence, which needs a place. Written so that the rival one seat early is genuinely attractive.

items.title: The Line That Makes Patients
items.theme: how moving a diagnostic threshold creates patients without anyone becoming iller
items.reviewer_notes: An opener item engineered so that each wrong slot is refused by a different feature: an unlicensed definite in the first sentence, a promised pair split from its pair, and an actor who arrives after the paragraph has finished with him.

items.title: Thirty, or Reasonable
items.theme: why the choice between a bright-line rule and an open standard is a trade rather than a safer option
items.reviewer_notes: The turn must come after the concession, not beside the claim it eventually defeats. 'That difference in visibility' in the following sentence is the confirming clue, and the paragraph's stance — even-handed, not pro-standard — is what the early slot destroys.

items.title: The Brother Who Was Not There
items.theme: why oral genealogies stay accurate about the present by quietly revising the past
items.reviewer_notes: The sentence carries a definite phrase of its own ('the new brother') as well as being needed by the last sentence's 'the charge of dishonesty'. Both clues point at the same seat, and the two early slots are attractive for different reasons.

items.title: Written Against Somebody
items.theme: a creed as the negative record of the positions its authors were refusing
items.reviewer_notes: Premium: the paragraph is thesis, evidence, two consequences, restatement, and three of the four slots are on topic. The decisive word is 'this' in the evidence sentence, which can only look backwards at a claim the evidence supports.

items.title: The Invitation at the Foot of the Page
items.theme: why the footnote was adopted by historians: an answer to rival accounts rather than a habit of pedantry
items.reviewer_notes: The paragraph runs past, past, past, hinge, present, present. The hinge is confirmed by 'It survives for that reason', which needs both a thing and a reason; the late slot is attractive and breaks the time frame by returning to the past after the paragraph has arrived in the present.

items.title: Practise Alone, Perform in Company
items.theme: why being watched helps a practised skill and harms one still being learnt
items.reviewer_notes: The paragraph offers a mechanism and then a two-branch consequence; the missing sentence is the branching step. The rival slot leaves 'That is why' pointing at a mechanism that explains a lift but not a split, which is the precise failure the item teaches.

items.title: Hung in the Order of a Life
items.theme: how a chronological retrospective manufactures a development the painter never had
items.reviewer_notes: The sentence contains 'thereby', which requires the mechanism to be on the page, and it supplies the circling that the following sentence concedes. The early slot is the trap a quick reader takes because the opening sentence invites a rebuttal at once.

items.title: The Promise on the Cover
items.theme: genre as a contract between reader and writer that decides what can count as a surprise
items.reviewer_notes: Built so that the most quotable slot is the wrong one: the sentence reads like a thesis and would open the paragraph happily were it not for 'works better', which needs the account it improves on, and for the definite 'the agreement' two sentences later.

items.title: The Price of Selling It Again
items.theme: why the resale market sets part of the price of a new durable good
items.reviewer_notes: An early-tier item where the decisive clue is a pairing in the last sentence — the expense and the discount as one fact seen twice — and the tempting slot is the one where the sentence would say the opening sentence over again in reverse.

items.title: Spend It by March
items.theme: how a rule that forbids carrying a budget forward manufactures the waste it was meant to prevent
items.reviewer_notes: The paragraph runs rule, rationale, effect, verdict, resistance, close. The verdict cannot precede the effect, because it says 'The waste', and the sentence about the obvious repair has officials agreeing where the fault lies — the naming and the agreement bracket the seat.

items.title: The Wall That Collected the Tolls
items.theme: why towns went on maintaining walls that had stopped being defences
items.reviewer_notes: An opener whose strongest rival is the closing slot, where the paragraph has already demolished the walls. Written so that the contradiction is a matter of dates rather than of tone.

items.title: Named Before the Numbers
items.theme: what lodging an analysis in advance actually certifies, and what it is mistaken for
items.reviewer_notes: The sentence carries its own restriction — a study that tests one named outcome — which is harmless in the middle of the paragraph and governs everything if the sentence opens it. The count 'exactly one thing' is picked up by 'That single guarantee' in the next sentence.

items.title: The Umbrella and Two Answers
items.theme: the difference between the cause of an action and the consideration acted on
items.reviewer_notes: The trap is a list: the sentence about causes ends with three of them, so a sentence saying 'only one of them can be contested' finds a false antecedent there. The closing 'That asymmetry' fixes the true seat.

items.title: Breathing After Dark
items.theme: why some desert plants take in gas at night and pay for it in growth
items.reviewer_notes: A problem-solution chain in which the missing sentence is the first move; the sentence after it says 'the hour the pores are open', which is the clue that fixes the seat, and the later storage sentence would repeat the night opening if the sentence were seated beyond it.

items.title: The News Nobody Wants to Carry
items.theme: why bad news travels slowly and arrives softened, and what an organisation would have to buy to prevent it
items.reviewer_notes: The prescription has to sit where a cause has just been given and where the next sentence can say 'the opposite of this'. The early slot is attractive to a reader who reaches for the practical upshot before the paragraph has supplied a mechanism.

items.title: Three Seconds to Take Over
items.theme: why an automated system that hands control back at the last moment redistributes blame rather than work
items.reviewer_notes: Defence, concession, turn, verdict, counter-concession, recommendation. The turn is the missing sentence; seated one slot early it makes the paragraph refute and then endorse, which is the failure the item teaches to hear.

items.title: The Hour Nobody Breaks
items.theme: why competing newsrooms honour an embargo, and what the exceptions reveal about the reason
items.reviewer_notes: The strongest wrong slot reads better forwards than the correct one does: it continues 'repeat player' with the access mechanism. It is refused only by looking backwards at 'That sanction', which courtesy cannot satisfy.

items.title: The Rent That Lets a Thing Start
items.theme: why old buildings house the enterprises that new buildings cannot afford to house
items.reviewer_notes: The clue in front is 'That difference', which needs two rents to have been compared. The strongest wrong slot pairs the sentence with the other half of the same comparison, where the paragraph is owed a conclusion rather than a premise.

items.title: The Sounds Still in the Spelling
items.theme: why English spelling preserves a pronunciation that stopped being spoken
items.reviewer_notes: The paragraph is present, past, past, hinge, present, present. 'Ever since' and 'the press' both point at the printing sentence, and the sentence after the gap speaks of 'the two' parting company, which needs the pair named.

items.title: As Deep as the Window Is High
items.theme: why old workrooms have tall windows and high ceilings, and why the rule is returning
items.reviewer_notes: An early-tier item whose wrong slots are all diagnosed by asking what 'That is why', 'for the same reason' and 'a different reason' would be pointing at; the correct seat is the only one that leaves all three pointing at the daylight rule.

items.title: Shouting at the Wrong Desk
items.theme: what happens to redress when complaint moves from the body that can remedy it to an audience that cannot
items.reviewer_notes: An opener that reads like a conclusion, which is what makes the middle slots tempting. The forward clue is 'The move', a definite phrase in the first visible sentence that nothing else licenses.

items.title: The Inspector Who Used to Build Them
items.theme: what an accusation of regulatory capture has to show, and why a biography is not it
items.reviewer_notes: The sentence is the paragraph's definition and its most quotable line, which is why the opening slot has to be argued away rather than dismissed. The forward clue is 'That test', which needs a criterion rather than a correction.

items.title: A Promise to the Dead
items.theme: why a promise made to someone now dead still binds, and what the obligation was attached to when it was made
items.reviewer_notes: An early-tier mid-gap: the sentence after the gap begins 'That is why', so the gap must be the explanation that sentence draws its conclusion from. The stance decoy concedes that the promise matters and then withdraws the duty, which is the one thing the paragraph is holding on to.

items.title: The Chamber That Cannot Win
items.theme: why a weaker second chamber survives: its authority depends on its inability to prevail
items.reviewer_notes: A premium opener. The decoy that calls the second chamber a survival with no job of its own fits the two sentences that follow it perfectly and is refused only by the third, which says what the arrangement actually produces. The broad constitutional opener is the trap for a reader who thinks the first sentence should be the biggest sentence.

items.title: The Advice You Would Give a Friend
items.theme: why the same decision is easier to settle when it belongs to somebody else, and what that licenses you to do
items.reviewer_notes: A paragraph that genuinely ends in a recommendation, so the correct option is the one that tells the reader what to do. The decoy about advisers is the same topic doing a different job, and the deliberation decoy contradicts the sentence that rules out information as the difference.

items.title: The Number That Protects the Absent
items.theme: the quorum as a guarantee given to the member who is not in the room, and what it fixes about attribution
items.reviewer_notes: The paragraph argues in the analytic present and hands the closer two things to bind: the reconstrual of the rule as a condition of validity, and the assurance given to the absent member. The historical decoy is fluent, relevant and in the wrong tense for a paragraph that has made no historical claim at all.

items.title: What the Ending Does to the Rest
items.theme: why a remembered ordeal is dominated by its worst moment and its last one rather than by how long it lasted
items.reviewer_notes: The sentence after the gap refers to 'the patients in the longer version', a term nothing before the gap has introduced. The gap must therefore propose the manipulation, and every option that draws the moral instead leaves that phrase unattached.

items.title: The Second Animal on the Island
items.theme: why removing one introduced species can release another that it had been holding down
items.reviewer_notes: The paragraph sets up a two-predator arrangement and the gap must say what happens when one of them is taken out first. The reversed-mechanism decoy is the near-tie: it describes a release, but of the wrong animal, and the sentence after the gap shows which way the release ran.

items.title: The Side That Pays Nothing
items.theme: why a market with two kinds of customer gives one side away, and the factual bet hidden in the decision
items.reviewer_notes: The sentence after the gap is an instance of a platform discovering it had subsidised the wrong half. The turn must therefore be about identifying the harder side, not about any other weakness of the arrangement, which is what the fragility decoy offers.

items.title: The Comment Under the Mark
items.theme: why written feedback goes unread when a grade is attached to it, and what follows for teachers who must also report
items.reviewer_notes: The gap must name the implication that the remedy after it acts on: comments and marks do different work and cannot travel together. The restatement decoy is a polished version of the sentence immediately above the gap and is the commonest wrong answer in the type.

items.title: The Repair You Are Meant to Find
items.theme: how a conservator's retouching settles a quarrel between the visitor's picture and the honesty of the record
items.reviewer_notes: The fourth sentence reports that the question is settled the same way everywhere, which rules out both the recap and the case-by-case ending: the closer must name one answer that satisfies the two stated demands at once. An earlier draft ended that sentence on an unsettleable quarrel, which left the recap defensible; a blind reader flagged it and it was tightened.

items.title: What Cannot Be Demanded
items.theme: the principle that an obligation presupposes an ability, and the narrower form it has to take to survive arranged inability
items.reviewer_notes: The sentence after the gap sorts two drivers: the one whose brakes fail is excused, the one who never had them checked is not. Only a restatement that moves the required ability to the moment the obligation was taken on can produce that sorting, which makes the gap tightly determined.

items.title: An Exception and a Counterexample
items.theme: the condition under which a case that a rule gets wrong is an exception rather than a refutation
items.reviewer_notes: The third sentence concedes that the shrug is not always a dodge, which obliges the gap to say when. The sentence after the gap supplies a test for the amended rule, so the gap must be a condition that such a test could operate on.

items.title: The Anniversary the Calendar Chose
items.theme: why public commemoration falls on round intervals, and whom the arithmetic shows such occasions to be addressed to
items.reviewer_notes: The sentence after the gap explains why commemorations thin as a generation thins and why a hundredth is a different kind of occasion. Only an implication about the audience can support both, which is what makes the decoy built on the number system's indifference detectable.

items.title: The Result You Already Know
items.theme: why a well-built experiment includes a condition whose outcome is settled in advance, and what a failure there means
items.reviewer_notes: The sentence after the gap says 'If nothing dies on that plate', which needs a plate to have been put on the bench. Two options now supply one, and the second supplies the wrong kind: a blind reader had solved an earlier draft by taking the only concrete option, so the untreated-plate decoy was written to remove that shortcut and make the direction of the control do the work.

items.title: The Words Nobody Translates
items.theme: why congregations keep a liturgical language they cannot construe, and what the unintelligibility performs
items.reviewer_notes: The sentence after the gap contrasts a vernacular prayer as something somebody wrote and can revise. That contrast only works if the gap has said what the old language secures: words received rather than composed. The music decoy is the named trap and is pleasant enough to be chosen by a reader who has stopped tracking the thread.

items.title: Four Means Something Went Wrong
items.theme: why a five-point rating scale collapses into two points, and what the platform reads instead
items.reviewer_notes: An opener for an analytic paragraph whose third sentence explicitly denies that the compression is a failure. The dismissive opener is the trap for a reader who matches topic and tone from the first two sentences only.

items.title: Published by Post
items.theme: why a letter to a learned society counted as publication, and what the practice had already supplied before journals existed
items.reviewer_notes: The paragraph's pivot is the third sentence, which says the register rather than the letter was the public thing. The decoy about printing being a convenience fits the fourth sentence and quietly contradicts that pivot, which is the local fit and global break in its cleanest form.

items.title: The Medicine That Makes Nothing Better
items.theme: why treatment for a condition with no symptoms is abandoned by patients who are attending carefully to how they feel
items.reviewer_notes: The fourth sentence dismisses forgetfulness and leaves a patient who is not forgetting anything. The closer must say what he is doing instead, and the paragraph has laid the answer out in its first two sentences: he is attending to evidence that has been arranged to point the wrong way.

items.title: The Polite Word Goes Blunt
items.theme: why a gentler substitute acquires the force of the word it replaced, and what that locates the offence in
items.reviewer_notes: The sentence after the gap begins with a conditional about where the offence is carried, which only makes sense if the gap has asked what is surviving the replacement. The historical decoy is fluent and in the past tense, which the paragraph's description of a recurring process never uses.

items.title: Eleven Minutes an Applicant
items.theme: why a policy is whatever the counter does with it, and what a reform that changes only the wording changes
items.reviewer_notes: The sentence after the gap explains what evaluations calling something implementation failure are really describing, which requires the gap to have said that a reform of the wording leaves the operative part untouched. The 'even so' decoy offers a remedy in the consequence slot and concedes against nothing.

items.title: Kin on One Side Only
items.theme: why counting descent through a single line removes a problem of competing claims, and what it cannot remove
items.reviewer_notes: The sentence after the gap reports elaborate arrangements for the line that is not counted, which can only be the consequence of a turn about that line continuing to exist. The property verdict is the premature close and is genuinely attractive, since the paragraph's first two sentences are about inheritance.

items.title: The Price of Paying as You Go
items.theme: why the same goods cost a poorer household more, and what that does to comparisons made in money
items.reviewer_notes: The closing sentence is about a threshold at which cheaper terms become available, which needs an implication about purchasing power rather than about market design. The broad sentiment is the primary trap and is the option most readers will feel is the right note to strike.

items.title: The Woman at the Bus Stop
items.theme: why the daily strangers we never speak to are missed when they disappear, and why speaking would spoil it
items.reviewer_notes: A foundation item with plain sentences and a genuine two-part puzzle: she is missed, and she cannot be greeted. The resolution has to cover both halves, which is what rules out the restatement and the warm generalisation.

items.title: The Same Answer, Arrived at Twice
items.theme: what the repeated appearance of one biological solution licenses, and what it does not say about the lineages
items.reviewer_notes: The sentence after the gap opens with 'That narrowness', which nothing before the gap supplies. Only a restatement that says how few answers the problem admits can bind it, which makes the slot tight despite the abstraction.

items.title: The Room You Walk Through
items.theme: how the corridor bought privacy for every room and quietly ended the meetings that used to happen by accident
items.reviewer_notes: An easy-tier qualification slot. The sentence after the gap reports that the household stopped meeting by accident, which is a cost; the option calling the change almost entirely a gain is therefore refused by the line that follows it rather than by anything subtle.

items.title: What the Case Turns Out to Have Decided
items.theme: why the binding part of a judgement is fixed by the courts that come after it, and what that does to a judge's reach
items.reviewer_notes: The sentence after the gap gives advice to a judge who wants to be followed, which requires an implication about who settles what a judgement decided. The reader-not-author option is the scope jump and is the most attractive wrong answer in the set.
